card.new_adaptation: Add a pending-plan state and payback gate to the EPLB controller. The first implementation uses a quiescent all-rank serving boundary for in-place migration: drain in-flight forwards and graph replays, agree on plan version and source map, migrate weights, verify each rank's destination rows, then publish the new map version before serving resumes. Before any weight mutation, timeout safely discards or defers the plan and leaves the old map active. After mutation starts, a failed collective must fail closed and recover from a known placement or restart; it cannot claim to roll back merely by restoring the old map. Shadow slots are an optional alternative only if measured free HBM supports them.

card.online_policy: Observable state: recent per-layer rank load and MoE step time, migration bytes and measured pause cost, queued prefills, active decodes, per-rank free HBM, and pending-plan age. Decision rule: at a safe boundary, commit only if estimated saved slow-rank time over a bounded horizon exceeds migration and queueing cost by a hysteresis margin; otherwise defer or discard at expiry. Action: either execute one versioned all-rank migration and publish the map, or keep the old placement. Overhead: host scoring, existing load collection, and measured coordination cost. Fallback: existing fixed placement or qualified async EPLB cadence. Strongest static comparator: best fixed placement and a capped rebalance schedule with equal expert memory.

card.new_adaptation: Add a pending-plan state and payback gate to the EPLB controller. The first implementation uses a quiescent all-rank serving boundary for in-place migration: drain in-flight forwards and graph replays, agree on plan version and source map, migrate weights, verify each rank's destination rows, then publish the new map version before serving resumes. Before any weight mutation, timeout safely discards or defers the plan and leaves the old map active. After mutation starts, a failed collective must fail closed and recover from a known placement or restart; it cannot claim to roll back merely by restoring the old map. Shadow slots are an optional alternative only if measured free HBM supports them.

card.online_policy: Observable state: recent per-layer rank load and MoE step time, migration bytes and measured pause cost, queued prefills, active decodes, per-rank free HBM, and pending-plan age. Action: either execute one versioned all-rank migration and publish the map, or keep the old placement. Overhead: host scoring, existing load collection, and measured coordination cost. Fallback: existing fixed placement or qualified async EPLB cadence. Strongest static comparator: best fixed placement and a capped rebalance schedule with equal expert memory.

A cap is simpler but cannot react to changing load; a host cadence replay is its cheapest comparison. Replica routing overlaps #59168 and needs redundant capacity; a memory and routing component check can rule it out. Retained commit timing with a quiescent, versioned in-place protocol and safe defer/discard before mutation.

Durable rank skew, migration payback, and support in either B200 layout are unmeasured.

card.mechanism: Keep an already computed expert-placement plan pending while prefill pressure or insufficient free HBM makes its migration expensive. Commit at a bounded later step when the predicted reduction in slow-rank MoE time exceeds migration and queueing cost. This acts on when EPLB moves weights, not on token routing or expert precision.
card.nearest_prior_art: PR #62009 adds asynchronous EPLB, fused MegaMoE mapping, and symmetric-memory migration for V4.1 on a larger GB200 topology. PR #61839 adds a rebalance cap on ROCm and reports costly migration. PR #59168 describes online placement and quota refresh. Those implementations are direct comparators, not evidence of transfer to the specified B200 node.
card.new_adaptation: Add a pending-plan state and a commit gate to the existing EPLB controller. Evaluate rank imbalance, pending-plan age, migration bytes, per-rank free HBM, and current prefill/decode pressure before all-rank commit. Keep the old expert map active until every rank acknowledges a complete migration; on timeout retain the old map and retry or discard the plan.

card.online_policy: Observable state: recent per-layer max/mean routed load, recent MoE step time, queued prefills, decode demand, migration bytes, free HBM per EP rank, and pending-plan age. Rule: commit only when an estimated payback within a bounded horizon clears a hysteresis margin and every rank has memory headroom; force a bounded decision at plan expiry. Action: migrate and atomically publish the new map at an all-rank boundary, or retain the current map. Overhead: existing load collection plus small host-side scoring and coordination; any added synchronization must be measured. Fallback: current static placement or existing async EPLB schedule. Strongest static comparator: best fixed EPLB configuration with the same redundant-expert memory budget.

card.mechanism: At completion of each cache block, distinguish an exact prefix already reused across turns from a newly computed suffix. Under KV pressure, admit proven reusable prefix blocks while putting one-use suffix blocks on probation. Promote a probationary block after a later exact-hash reuse. This targets TTFT and cache capacity for repeated agent histories with changing tool output. The target's 75% cacheability is a goal, not a measured hit rate.
card.nearest_prior_art: PR #51981 provides per-request no-store while preserving reads; RR-Evict spreads eviction across agent histories; PRs #54625 and #58837 reorder admission around resident prefixes. The proposed behavior changes cache writes at block granularity and requires a separate comparison with each.
card.new_adaptation: Add a bounded per-prefix reuse table and a probation state to the local block-pool commit path. A complete block receives normal cache residency only after repeat use, except for a bounded protected shared-prefix budget. Preserve content hashes and never treat speculative or incomplete blocks as committed. The novel implementation claim is conditional until the pinned scheduler and hybrid V4.1 cache lifecycle are inspected.

novelty.deployment: Unestablished on the specified B200 DEP8 or two DEP4 layouts; the supplied 75% target is not an observed cache-hit rate.
novelty.implementation: Potential block-level adaptation beyond #51981's request-level switch; pinned-baseline inclusion and overlap with other cache policies remain unverified.
novelty.publication: Unestablished. RR-Evict, PEEK, and existing cache-admission work already cover closely related policy space.

card.online_policy: Observable state: exact block-hash repeat count, block completion, free-block pressure, waiting requests' matched prefixes, and per-session cached-prefix coverage. Rule: at low pressure use current admission; at pressure admit repeated hashes and bounded shared ancestors, probationarily decline new private suffix writes; age probation entries and revert to ordinary admission if reuse evidence is sparse. Action affects optional cache retention only, never active KV required for generation. Overhead is hash-table bookkeeping on block commit plus bounded eviction work. Fallback is current cache admission. Strongest static comparator is PR #51981-style per-request no-store supplied by the application, alongside stock LRU.
card.readiness: Design and CPU replay are plausible now; integration readiness is low until V4.1 cache-group commit semantics and active prefix-cache behavior are checked.
card.revision_after_critique: Explored three mechanisms: request-level no-store activation (#51981), round-robin tail eviction (RR-Evict), and block-level probation. The first two are comparators; retained probation because it adds specific per-block write behavior. Narrowed the claim to optional local cache retention and made exact reuse, pressure, and cold-request latency decisive measurements.

rubric.correctness: Exact committed-block hashes, active-block pinning, cancellation, and prefix-hit versus cold output parity are required.
rubric.cost: Low CPU-screen cost; moderate code work; eight-GPU serving cost is unestimated.
rubric.distinctness: Different from request-level no-store and queue reordering; closely related to RR-Evict and PEEK.
rubric.evidence: Prior cache policies support the failure mode, but supplied evidence has no target trace.
rubric.experiment: Start with CPU replay of frozen request hashes and cache capacity; promote to matched serving A/B only if it reduces recomputed prompt tokens.
rubric.integration: Medium-to-high complexity because hybrid cache groups, speculative tokens, and eviction references must stay coherent.
rubric.mechanism: Optional block-write admission at commit time, with exact-hash promotion and pressure fallback.
rubric.research_contribution: Potential workload-specific policy result; publication novelty is unestablished.
rubric.value: Conditional TTFT-tail and prefill-work opportunity for recurring agent prefixes; no B200 gain established.

card.strongest_objection: The candidate may discard exactly the suffix needed by the next agent turn. A per-request no-store hint or RR-Evict may achieve the same benefit with less scheduler work. No supplied B200 request/block trace establishes cache thrashing, avoidable misses, or a performance gain.
